newsitem.title: UK: W.African crude steady, Asian July buying muted.
newsitem.headline: W.African crude steady, Asian July buying muted.

text.p: West African crude differentials were steady to slightly firmer in mostly slow discussion on Wednesday, traders said.
Far East buyers who have taken large amounts of West African in recent weeks have filled most of their requirements and much July had now been placed, they said.
"There is very little Nigerian left on an fob basis for July," a trader said, adding that while there was plenty of third decade left it would probably be heading to final destinations on co-loaders.

Traders said they had heard that a late July loading Forcados changed hands at a premium in the low 20 cents above Dated Brent on Tuesday. A Bonny Light was also heard moving at a premium in the mid-40s over Dated Brent.
In recent Asian action, a Korean buyer was heard taking an Odudu/Qua Iboe to the Far East. Japanese buyers were rumoured to be looking for a Forcados, a Light Medium and two Penningtons.
A Bonny Light loading July 16-17 moved on Monday at dated +45 cents. A third decade Bonny Light changed hands at between 43 and 45 cents over Dated.
A Forcados was done on Monday at 23 cents over Dated Brent. Brass River, done last week at a rumoured high 40s over Dated, is offered at around 50 cents over Dated.
